questions.question: What will be the annual payment of a loan of Rs 1,200 payable in 2 years at 8(1)/(3)% compound interest rate?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Rate = 8(1)/(3)% = 1/12. Ratio of Principal to Installment for Year 1 = 12 : 13.

For Year 2, the ratio is 12² : 13² = 144 : 169.

Equating installments (making them 169), Year 1 ratio becomes (12 × 13) : (13 × 13) = 156 : 169.

Total Principal = 156 + 144 = 300 parts.

Given 300 parts = Rs. 1200 ⇒ 1 part = 4.

Annual installment = 169 parts × 4 = Rs. 676.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 676.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Loan Amount (P) = Rs. 1200

Rate of Interest (R) = 8&frac{1}{3}% = 25/3% ⇒ Fractional value = 1/12

Time = 2 years

Let each equal annual payment be x.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e46fd4a99e6c54ccf19a59612e321d94ca031d71ebaeec6081ad705f82609c46.png] 

**Formula Used:**

P = x / (1 + R/100) + x / (1 + R/100)²

**Calculations:**

⇒ 1200 = x / (1 + 1/12) + x / (1 + 1/12)²

⇒ 1200 = x / (13/12) + x / (13/12)²

⇒ 1200 = (12x / 13) + (144x / 169)

⇒ 1200 = (156x + 144x) / 169

⇒ 1200 = 300x / 169

⇒ x = (1200 × 169) / 300

⇒ x = 4 × 169

⇒ x = 676

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 676.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Installment

For a loan P paid in n equal annual installments x at rate R: P = x/(1+R/100) + x/(1+R/100)² + ... + x/(1+R/100)ⁿ

Simple Interest Installment

The annual payment x that will discharge a debt A due in n years at simple interest rate R is: x = (100 × A) ÷ [100n + n(n−1)R/2]

Effective Compound Interest Rate for 2 Years

The net effective rate for 2 years at R% per annum is given by: (2R + R²/100)%

questions.question: A sum of money triples itself at compound interest in 10 years. In how many years will it become nine times.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A sum of money triples itself at compound interest in 10 years.

**Formula used:**

Amount = principle[1 + dfrac{rate}{100}]time

**Calculations:**

Amount after 10 years,

3 principle = prinicple[1 + dfrac{rate}{100}]¹⁰

3 = [1 + dfrac{rate}{100}]¹⁰ (eqn1)

Now, when it becomes nine times

9 principle = principle[1 + dfrac{rate}{100}]time

3² = [1 + dfrac{rate}{100}]time

[1 + dfrac{rate}{100}]time = {(1 + dfrac{rate}{100})¹⁰}² (putting the value of eqn1)

Time = 10 × 2 = 20 years

**∴ The answer is 20 years.**

questions.question: The compound interest (compounding half yearly) received on Rs. 2200 for 1.5 years is Rs. 3836.8. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Amount (A) = ₹2200 + ₹3836.8 = ₹6036.8

Amount to Principal Ratio = 6036.8 ÷ 2200 = 60368 ÷ 22000 = 343 ÷ 125

For 3 half-years, Multiplying factor = ³√(343 ÷ 125) = 7 ÷ 5

Rate per half-year = (7 − 5) ÷ 5 × 100% = 40%

Rate per annum = 40% × 2 = 80%

**∴ The correct answer is 80%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹2200

Time (T) = 1.5 years ⇒ n = 3 half-years

Compound Interest (CI) = ₹3836.8

Amount (A) = P + CI = 2200 + 3836.8 = ₹6036.8

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R ÷ 100)ⁿ

Where R is the rate per period and n is the number of periods.

 
 P = ₹2200
 
 
 A = ₹6036.8
 
 

 

 
 3 Half-Years
 CI = ₹3836.8

**Calculations:**

⇒ 6036.8 = 2200 × (1 + R ÷ 100)³

⇒ 6036.8 ÷ 2200 = (1 + R ÷ 100)³

⇒ 60368 ÷ 22000 = (1 + R ÷ 100)³

⇒ 343 ÷ 125 = (1 + R ÷ 100)³

⇒ (7 ÷ 5)³ = (1 + R ÷ 100)³

⇒ 1 + R ÷ 100 = 7 ÷ 5

⇒ R ÷ 100 = 7 ÷ 5 − 1 = 2 ÷ 5

⇒ R = 2 ÷ 5 × 100 = 40%

⇒ The rate per half-year is 40%.

⇒ Annual Rate = 40% × 2 = 80%

**∴ The correct answer is 80%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the annual interest rate is halved, and the total number of periods becomes twice the number of years.

Quarterly Compounding

When interest is compounded quarterly, the annual interest rate is divided by 4, and the total number of periods becomes four times the number of years.

Effective Annual Rate (EAR)

If the half-yearly rate is R%, the effective annual interest rate due to compounding can be calculated using the formula: (2R + R² ÷ 100)%.

questions.question: A man wants to invest Rs. 40,440 in bank account of his two sons whose age were 12 years and 16 years in such a way that they will get equal amount at age of 20 years @ 33(1)/(3)% per annum compounded annually. Find the share of younger son?
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Principal = Rs. 40440

Ages of sons = 12 years and 16 years

Rate of interest = 33(1)/(3)% per annum compounded annually.

**FORMULA USED:**

 A = P (1+ r/100)ⁿ

**CALCULATION:**

Let the principal for younger son be Rs x

Principal for elder son be Rs y

Interest to be calculated for

Younger son = (20 – 12) = 8 years

Elder son = (20 – 16) = 4 years

Since, amount will be equally distributed then,

⇒ x(1 + 100/300)⁸ = y (1 + 100/300)⁴

⇒ x(4/3)⁸ = y(4/3)⁴

⇒ (4/3)⁽⁸ ⁻ ⁴⁾ = y/x

⇒ y/x = 256/81

∴ Younger son’s share = 81/337 × 40,440 = Rs. 9,720

questions.question: At what rate of interest compound interest per annum will Rs. 640 amount to Rs. 774.40 in 2 years
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs 640

Amount = Rs 774.40

Time = 2 years

**Concept:**

A = P (1 + R/100)n

**Calculation:**

Let rate = R%

By using the formula,

⇒ A = P (1 + R/100)ⁿ

⇒ 774.40 = 640 (1 + R/100)² 

⇒ (1 + R/100)² = 774.40/640

⇒ (1 + R/100)² = 484/400

⇒ (1 + R/100)² = (22/20)²

⇒ By cancelling the powers on both sides, (1 + R/100) = (22/20)

⇒ R/100 = 22/20 – 1 = (22 - 20)/20 = 2/20

⇒ R = 100/10 = **10%**

∴ Required Rate is 10% per annum.

questions.question: Find the amount payable on maturity if ₹20,00,000 is invested at 12% per annum for (3)/(2) years and interest is compounded half-yearly.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For half-yearly compounding, new rate = 12% ÷ 2 = 6%, time = 3/2 × 2 = 3 cycles.

Effective compound interest rate for 3 cycles at 6% = 3r . 3r² . r³ = 18 . 108 . 216 → 19.1016%

Compound Interest = 19.1016% of ₹20,00,000 = ₹3,82,032

Total Amount = Principal + CI = 20,00,000 + 3,82,032 = ₹23,82,032

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23,82,032.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹20,00,000

Rate of Interest (R) = 12% p.a.

Time (T) = 3/2 years

**Formula Used:**

Amount (A) = P(1 + r/100)ⁿ

Where r is the rate per period, and n is the number of periods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/acc683e8a0f9a1355ec5fb7f0a07b1b41b33700b10c58dd6d16945e1ad4ecd0e.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest is compounded half-yearly, so rate per period (r) = 12% ÷ 2 = 6%

⇒ Number of cycles (n) = 3/2 × 2 = 3

⇒ A = 2000000 × (1 + 6/100)³

⇒ A = 2000000 × (106/100)³

⇒ A = 2000000 × (53/50) × (53/50) × (53/50)

⇒ A = 2000000 × 148877 / 125000

⇒ A = 16 × 148877

⇒ A = 23,82,032

**∴ The correct answer is ₹23,82,032.**

**__Additional Information__**

Half-Yearly Compounding Adjustment

When interest is compounded half-yearly, the principal is updated every 6 months. Therefore, the annual rate (R) is halved (R/2) and the time (T in years) is multiplied by 2 (2T).

Effective CI Rate for 3 Periods

For a uniform interest rate of r%, the effective compound interest over 3 periods can be quickly found using the formula: 3r + 3r²/100 + r³/10000.

Multiplier Factor Method

Instead of calculating standard percentages, the Final Amount can be derived by repeatedly multiplying the Principal with the fractional scaling factor (1 + r/100) successively for n periods.

Successive increase = x + x + x²/100

So,

After 3 years amount = 125x × 9/5 × 8/5 × 3/5

⇒ 216x

So, Intereset = 216x - 125x = 91

Cumulative rate of interest = 91/125 × 100 = 72.8%

From option,

Again 44 + 20 + (44 × 20)/100 = 72.8%

questions.question: ₹1,20,000 becomes ₹1,50,528 in two years at a certain rate of compound interest, compounding annually in an investment scheme. In the same scheme, the sum of ₹P is invested and it becomes ₹3,51,232 in three years. What is the value of P?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Growth factor for **two years** = 1,50,528 ÷ 1,20,000 = 1.2544

Annual growth factor = √1.2544 = 1.12

For **three years**, the sum **₹P** grows by a factor of 1.12³ = 1.404928

∴ P = 3,51,232 ÷ 1.404928 = 2,50,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,50,000.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Case 1: Principal (P₁) = **₹1,20,000**, Amount (A₁) = **₹1,50,528**, Time (t₁) = **2 years**

Case 2: Principal (P₂) = **₹P**, Amount (A₂) = **₹3,51,232**, Time (t₂) = **3 years**

**Formula Used:**

Compound Interest Amount, A = P(1 + r/100)t

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00a3cf16098696a94a77c9634b346a9a75ba15a8598789c137411347f7a07aaa.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ For the first investment: 1,50,528 = 1,20,000 × (1 + r/100)²

⇒ (1 + r/100)² = 1,50,528 ÷ 1,20,000 = 1.2544

⇒ 1 + r/100 = √1.2544 = 1.12

⇒ For the second investment: 3,51,232 = P × (1.12)³

⇒ 3,51,232 = P × 1.404928

⇒ P = 3,51,232 ÷ 1.404928

⇒ P = 2,50,000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹2,50,000.**

**__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount A after t years is given by A = P(1 + r/100)t, where P is the principal and r is the annual interest rate.

Growth Multiplier

The term (1 + r/100) is the annual multiplying factor. If a sum grows for n years, the total multiplier is (1 + r/100)ⁿ.

Effective Rate of Interest

For a rate r compounded annually for 2 years, the effective interest rate is calculated as [r + r + (r × r)/100]%.
